The question of using AI confounding creators and composers, artists and illustrators, poets and writers a like is - to paraphrase Syndrone from The Incredibles: "When everyone is creative, will anyone be?" Am I the patron or the artist to the work created by the AI agent?

There is l'art pour l'art, the avent garde, where artist press boundaries . But often at limited expense. Paints and brushes, pens and paper, stone and clay. Commerical success was -- and deamed selling out. Will -- when a few golden prompts create an image 

Or, in a commercial sense, if anyone can create anything, who will someone pay to see anyone elses creation?  

I understand Hollywood producers seeking to reduce the size of budgets by switching to new technologies. I understand Hollywood creators seeking to protect their livelihood in the wake of seismic changes to the industry. Perhaps each party grasps: who will want to pay for what others create when a personalized AI agent can create their own story. For creators relying on million dollar salaries that need hundreds of millions from distributing the films to be profitable and be able to make the next movie. Each entertainment dollar directed to personalized content diminishes the budget for the next Hollywood production.

Will we enter a world where entertainment whether video or film is best paraphrased by Winston Churchill: "Never was so much created by so many but viewed by so few"?
